caption: The drawing depicts an architectural entrance featuring a prominent archway constructed from alternating red and white segments, with wooden beams visible at the top within the arch. The arch is supported on both sides by square pillars, each comprised of reddish rectangular bricks with white mortar lines and a light stone base. Beneath the arch is a wooden double door with a wavy vertical grain pattern, framed by a decorative white and red rectangular molding. Above the door, there is a semi-circular pediment, also in white and red, supported by short columns at each end. The wall behind the doorway is light yellow and shaded with pale blue and ochre, featuring a painted alcove at the center top with red, shell-like detailing inside, flanked by symmetrical painted designs of vases with stylized flowers and scrollwork in soft reds and blues. The floor is composed of reddish-brown tiles arranged in a regular rectangular pattern. The background is plain, with the details of the archway and entrance in the foreground, and the drawing is rendered in watercolor or a similar medium, with soft, blended edges and visible texture.
title: Restoration Drawing: Main Doorway & Arch to Mission House
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
